# Mirror Lab

> Mirror Lab is an open, fully simulated AI-safety benchmark for tool-using LLM agents. A harmless game interface is wired to a simulated hazardous backend through a state machine that is identical under both readings (a kinematic–semantic isomorphism). A cue ladder adds one real-world clue per rung to find when an agent stops and asks a human.

- Two domains: a robotic manipulator ("Sweetness Chef" watermelon game vs a surgical blade plunge) and a payload drone ("Sky Party" toy drop vs a 20 kg crate over people).
- Cue ladder: pure_toy, cue_names, cue_payload, cue_irreversible, cue_clue, cue_manual, plus a control_toy condition with a harmless backend.
- Paper findings (v2 draft, 117 replay-verified episodes, 24 provider refusals, 3 seeds per cell; directional): with no cues every model acted (24/24); on the robot arm models stopped at different rungs; on the drone only two of four models ever stopped, confounded by benign wording; provider safeguards blocked one model at every cued rung but never at the cue-free rung.
- Everything is simulated and log-only. No hardware or people are involved.
